battle.name: 第二次鱈魚戰爭
battle.theater: 冰島近海與北大西洋漁場
battle.brief: 第二次鱈魚戰爭是冰島與英國、西德等國在北大西洋就鱈魚漁場與海界劃界引發的海上對抗，衝突以皇家海軍護漁艦、警戒艦與北歐漁船的對峙及追逐為主，期間亦以婆塞德後膛砲（Breech-loading cannon，1870年）等艦載後膛火砲執行警告射擊與海上警戒。

kit.name: 婆塞德後膛砲
kit.history: 婆塞德後膛砲是十九世紀德國海軍沿岸與近海警戒船隻採用的後膛火砲，屬艦載岸防型別，負責近岸防禦與警告射擊，非主力艦砲。

countries: 本役的實際交戰方是冰島與英國，雙方都沒有宣戰，也沒有把事件當作正式國際戰爭處理。冰島沒有常備海軍，由冰島海岸防衛隊在政府授權下執行漁業管轄，使用遠洋巡邏艇在其主張的五十海里經濟區攔截英籍拖網漁船；英國則由皇家海軍北大西洋艦隊及漁業保護部隊護送漁船。冰島與英國同屬北大西洋公約組織，美國、西德等盟國沒有加入交戰，只透過外交與盟內管道要求克制。行動集中於冰島東岸、東北方及北側外海。題名所列的「1972」是背景年份：冰島於一九七二年擴張管轄權，並在十一月發生一次前置碰撞；實際的警告射擊與延續至六月的海上對抗始於一九七三年二月十一日，因此通常稱為一九七三年的第二次鱈魚戰爭。
countriesEn: The actual belligerents in this conflict were Iceland and the United Kingdom, although neither side declared war or treated the confrontation as a formally constituted international war. Iceland had no standing navy, so the Icelandic Coast Guard enforced the fisheries jurisdiction claimed by its government, using oceangoing patrol vessels to intercept British trawlers inside Iceland's asserted fifty-nautical-mile economic zone. Britain relied on the Royal Navy's North Atlantic forces and its fisheries-protection units to escort the trawlers. Iceland and Britain were both members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, but the United States, West Germany, and the other allies did not join the fighting and instead pressed for restraint through diplomatic channels. Operations were concentrated east, northeast, and north of Iceland. The year 1972 in the title refers to the background: Iceland expanded its jurisdictional claims that year, and a preliminary collision occurred in November. The recorded warning fire and the sustained maritime confrontation beginning on 11 February 1973 and ending in June are therefore normally called the Second Cod War of 1973.
people: 英國方面，首相愛德華·希思批准皇家海軍保護漁船，早期外交處理主要由外相詹姆斯·卡拉漢負責，四月後則由安東尼·克羅斯蘭接手；海軍部與北大西洋艦隊的指揮官決定任務編組、護航航線及交火限制。冰島方面，總理Ólafur Jóhannesson主持國防與漁業政策，海岸防衛隊的巡邏艇長、輪機人員及射手則在近岸交鋒中掌握實際節奏。五月二十九日，冰島船Þór與英國護衛艦HMS Intrepid相撞，海岸防衛隊員Halldór Hallfreðsson死亡，這是有清楚姓名紀錄的作戰死亡。Þór船長Ólafur Ólafsson其後被控過失殺人，法庭判定其未能成立，因而判他無罪。英籍漁船與海軍艦艇上的船長、軍官和輪機人員則負責維持魚汛作業、追蹤、雷達觀察與維修。
peopleEn: On the British side, Prime Minister Edward Heath authorized the Royal Navy to protect the trawlers. Foreign Secretary James Callaghan handled the initial diplomatic response, after which Anthony Crosland took over in April. The Admiralty and the commanders of the North Atlantic force determined the task organization, escort routes, and restrictions on the use of force. On the Icelandic side, Prime Minister Ólafur Jóhannesson directed defense and fisheries policy, while the commanders, engineers, and gunners of the Coast Guard exercised practical control during close encounters. On 29 May, the Icelandic vessel Þór collided with the British frigate HMS Intrepid, and Coast Guard member Halldór Hallfreðsson was killed; his death is the combat fatality for which a clear personal record survives. Ólafur Ólafsson, the captain of Þór, was later charged with manslaughter, but the court did not find his conduct negligent and acquitted him. The masters, officers, and engineering personnel aboard the British trawlers and naval vessels were responsible for continuing fishing operations, tracking contacts, radar observation, and maintenance.
kits: 英方海上骨幹包括Type 21級輕護衛艦HMS Intrepid，該艦於一九七二年服役；Type 42飛彈驅逐艦HMS Bristol；以及Centaur級輕型航空母艦HMS Bulwark。Type 21與Type 42均以單裝4.5吋Mk 6主炮為主要重火力，HMS Bulwark亦配有4.5吋砲位，其航空組使用Westland Sea King反潛直昇機執行搜索、偵察和通訊中繼。海軍航空兵力主要負責搜索與監視，而非對冰島巡邏艇直接攻擊。冰方以Ægir、Þór、Óðinn、Freyja及Esja等數百噸至約千噸級的遠洋巡邏艇為核心，其中多數源自北歐海岸防衛或巡查船，主要砲火為40公厘Bofors自動砲，部分艇另有小口徑快砲及機槍。英籍拖網船則配有柴油主機、拖網絞機、繩網作業裝置、探魚器及船岸無線電。英軍由油輪和補給艦維持燃料、 food、淡水與備件，冰方則由沿岸基地補充40公厘砲彈、燃油及維修材料；兩套後勤體系在作戰半徑與補給週期上差距明顯。
kitsEn: The British surface force was built around the light frigate HMS Intrepid of the Type 21 class, commissioned in 1972; the Type 42 guided-missile destroyer HMS Bristol; and the Centaur-class light fleet carrier HMS Bulwark. The Type 21 and Type 42 ships carried a single 4.5-inch Mark 6 gun as their principal heavy armament, while HMS Bulwark also had 4.5-inch gun positions and operated Westland Sea King anti-submarine helicopters for search, reconnaissance, and communications relay. The naval air effort was principally concerned with surveillance and hunting rather than direct attacks on Icelandic patrol craft. Iceland's core force consisted of oceangoing cutters Ægir, Þór, Óðinn, Freyja, and Esja, ranging from several hundred tons to roughly a thousand tons. Most were converted from northern European coastguard or patrol vessels, with 40 mm Bofors automatic cannon as their main armament; some also carried smaller automatic cannon and machine guns. British trawlers were equipped with diesel engines, trawl winches, net-handling gear, echo sounders, and ship-to-shore radios. British fuel, food, fresh water, ammunition, and spare parts were maintained by fleet tankers and stores ships, whereas Icelandic cutters replenished 40 mm ammunition, fuel, and maintenance items from shore bases. The difference in endurance and resupply range was immediately apparent.
tactics: 冰方採取沿岸防守結合海上截擊的作法。岸上觀察站先發現漁船與護衛艦，海岸防衛隊再由港口向北、東方向出航，利用數量較多但排水量較小的艇隻逼近，以船艏橫置、警告射擊、要求停船檢查及碰撞拖離等手段阻止拖網。掩護艦接近時，冰方艇隻常反覆改變航向，把英方漁船與護衛艦分隔，並利用岸基電報回報位置。英方則把漁船編成伴隨隊，由Type 21護衛艦、Type 42驅逐艦及較大型平台在漁船外側形成巡邏屏障，以航速、排水量和較長航程持續跟蹤。必要時，英艦直接插入冰方巡邏艇與漁船之間，以艦艏推擠、迫使對方退出或協助拖走受損漁船；Sea King則擴大雷達觀察及通訊範圍。英方主要射擊仍限於警告與防禦，4.5吋砲沒有被確認用來蓄意瞄準冰方艦艇。雙方都不正式宣告擊沉對方船隻，結果雖有碰撞與重複警告射擊，仍沒有戰艦或漁船被確認擊沉。
tacticsEn: Iceland employed a combination of coastal defense and maritime interception. Shore observation stations first reported fishing vessels and escorts, after which the Coast Guard sailed north and east from Icelandic ports. Its smaller but more numerous craft used speed and local initiative to close the distance, place their bows across the trawlers' course, fire warning shots, call on the vessels to stop for inspection, and use collision or towing pressure to make them haul away. When escorts approached, Icelandic cutters repeatedly altered course to separate the trawlers from their protectors and reported their positions by radio to shore stations. Britain organized the trawlers into escorted groups, with Type 21 frigates, Type 42 destroyers, and larger ships patrolling outside the fishing vessels. The warships used their speed, size, and endurance to shadow the Icelandic cutters, insert themselves between a cutter and a trawler, shoulder the smaller vessel aside, force it to withdraw, and assist in towing damaged boats. Sea King helicopters extended radar observation and communications coverage. British gunfire remained primarily defensive or warning-oriented, and there is no confirmed deliberate use of the 4.5-inch guns against Icelandic ships. Neither side formally announced an intention to sink the other's vessels. Despite collisions and repeated warning fire, neither a warship nor a trawler was confirmed sunk.
data: 一九七二年十月十五日，冰島把經濟區主張由十二海里擴至五十海里；十一月九日，海岸防衛艇Óðinn與英籍拖網船Apollo相撞，雙方受損，英方指稱遭到故意衝撞，冰方則認為碰撞不能單方面歸責。英國漁船因此在之後數週避開爭議區域。一九七三年二月十一日，Ægir對一艘英國漁船發射警告砲彈，成為第二次鱈魚戰爭公開對抗的起點；二月中旬，英方開始派遣皇家海軍並組織護航。英國護航編隊由英國本土沿北海北上，主要在冰島東北方漁場及五十海里界線附近攔截，冰方則由沿岸基地往返巡邏。月底至四月，雙方記錄了警告射擊、查船、拖船、漁船與巡邏艇相撞，以及護衛艦與冰方艇隻互相施壓的事件；英冰雙方日誌對每次接觸由誰挑起及是否故意常有不同表述。五月為英方兵力高峰，海上任務兵力約四十艘，Bulwark在較外側區域支援，Type 21與Type 42護衛兵力則貼近漁船隊。五月二十九日，Þór與HMS Intrepid在追截糾纏中重撞，兩船均受損，Halldór Hallfreðsson死亡。六月一日起，海上的警告射擊、碰撞與強制攔截實際停止。
dataEn: On 15 October 1972, Iceland extended its claimed economic zone from twelve to fifty nautical miles. On 9 November, the Coast Guard cutter Óðinn collided with the British trawler Apollo, damaging both vessels; Britain alleged a deliberate ramming, while Iceland rejected sole responsibility for the collision. British trawlers consequently avoided the disputed area for several weeks. On 11 February 1973, Ægir fired a warning round across the bow of a British trawler, marking the start of the openly recorded confrontation in the Second Cod War. In mid-February, Britain began deploying the Royal Navy and organizing escorts. The British escort force sailed north from the United Kingdom along the North Sea and operated mainly near the fishing grounds northeast of Iceland and around the fifty-mile boundary, while Icelandic cutters shuttled between coastal bases and the patrol area. From late February through April, the records contain warning fire, attempted inspections, towing, collisions between fishing vessels and cutters, and repeated pressure between escorts and Icelandic boats. British and Icelandic logs often differed over who initiated an encounter and whether it was intentional. British deployment peaked in May at approximately forty vessels. HMS Bulwark operated farther offshore while Type 21 and Type 42 escorts remained close to the trawler groups. On 29 May, Þór and HMS Intrepid collided heavily during an interception, both were damaged, and Halldór Hallfreðsson was killed. On 1 June, warning fire, collisions, and forcible interceptions in the maritime confrontation ceased in practice.
cause: 第二次鱈魚戰爭不是單一事故引發，而是英冰漁業管轄矛盾長期累積的結果。一九五八至一九六一年第一次鱈魚戰爭期間，冰島把領海範圍擴至十二海里，英國以海軍維護漁船作業，衝突最後才由雙邊協議暫時控制。戰後安排只提供有限而限期的英國准入權，沒有永久解決五十海里內由誰管轄、漁船能在何處作業的問題。七十年代初，海洋資源管轄逐漸成為北歐國家政策核心；冰島於一九七二年主動把經濟區擴至五十海里，英國反對承認這項單方面變更，理由是其漁船長期依賴冰島附近漁場，並認為既有談判權利不應被新宣告取代。西德漁船也依賴相同漁場，因此同樣反對冰島立即擴張。十一月Óðinn與Apollo的碰撞使外交爭端升溫，而英冰對事件責任、警告射擊性質及海上執法權限各執一詞。冰島相信小型海岸防衛隊能憑地理、港口與法律管轄限制英方作業，英方則認為若不部署海軍，漁船會持續遭攔截，於是兩國都得到政治理由維持對抗。
causeEn: The Second Cod War was the product of a long accumulation of Anglo-Icelandic disputes over fisheries jurisdiction rather than the consequence of one isolated accident. During the First Cod War of 1958 to 1961, Iceland extended its territorial sea to twelve nautical miles, while Britain used the Royal Navy to protect fishing operations; the conflict was finally contained through a bilateral agreement. The postwar arrangements granted British access only on a limited and temporary basis and did not permanently settle who would regulate fishing inside fifty miles or where trawlers could work. In the early 1970s, jurisdiction over marine resources became a central northern European policy issue. Iceland unilaterally expanded its economic zone to fifty nautical miles in 1972. Britain opposed recognition of the change, arguing that its fleet depended on the fishing grounds around Iceland and that existing negotiated access rights could not simply be displaced by a unilateral declaration. West German trawlers also relied on the same grounds and therefore opposed Iceland's immediate extension. The collision between Óðinn and Apollo in November heightened the diplomatic dispute, while Britain and Iceland disagreed over responsibility for the collision, the nature of the warning fire, and the respective authority to enforce fishing restrictions. Iceland believed that a small coastguard, supported by geography, ports, and a jurisdictional claim, could deny British vessels access more cheaply than a fleet confrontation. Britain concluded that without naval protection its trawlers would continue to be intercepted and that sustained deployments were therefore politically necessary.
impact: 海上結果受到控制，但政治與法律影響很大。整場衝突沒有英國軍艦被確認擊沉，也沒有可靠紀錄顯示漁船被擊沉；損失集中在碰撞造成的船體修理、拖網與其他漁具損壞，以及漁船退出五十海里區域所造成的停捕。傷亡方面，有姓名及事故報告支持的是Halldór Hallfreðsson一人死亡，英方初報中其餘非致命傷者數字並不一致，本實錄不列未經核實的精確人數。英方以數十艘艦艇、空中搜索和長距離補給維持存在，顯示海軍能控制接觸頻率，卻不能單靠艦砲迫使冰島放棄管轄主張。事件也令兩個北大西洋公約盟國之間出現嚴重外交摩擦，美國與其他盟國均要求避免軍事化，最終沒有使用公約第五條。對冰島而言，小型海岸防衛隊、港口基地與近海地理被證明足以向英國漁船施加停捕成本；對英國而言，它們則證明護航能降低漁船損失，卻無法迫使冰島接受英方對五十海里的權利觀。
impactEn: The maritime outcome remained limited, but the political and legal consequences were substantial. No British warship was confirmed sunk, and no reliable record shows that a fishing vessel was sunk. The losses instead took the form of collision damage, repairs to trawlers and cutters, damage to trawls and other fishing gear, and the interruption of fishing while vessels withdrew from the fifty-mile area. Halldór Hallfreðsson is the one death supported by a name and an accident report. The numbers of non-fatal British casualties differed among early summaries, so no unverified exact figure is given here. Britain's use of several dozen warships, aerial search, and long-range supply kept the Royal Navy present and reduced the frequency with which isolated trawlers could be intercepted, but naval gunfire could not force Iceland to abandon its jurisdictional claim. The dispute also created serious friction between two NATO allies. The United States and the other members urged military restraint, and Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty was never invoked. Iceland demonstrated that a small coastguard, coastal bases, and proximity to home ports could impose a substantial cost on British fishing by compelling vessels to suspend operations. Britain demonstrated that escorting warships could reduce damage to its fleet, but could not make Iceland accept the British interpretation of the fifty-mile limit.
result: 六月一日的實際停鬥沒有帶來任何一方全面貫徹的海上勝負。冰島在五十海里內的實質執法地位得以維持，英籍漁船則在衝突期間大多撤出該區或只在護航下有限作業；英國任務兵力隨後撤離或轉向其他部署。停鬥同日，英國宣布建立自身的二百海里漁業保護區，冰島也把政策推向二百海里管轄，雙方再把漁業爭端帶入國際法院程序。法院先處理管轄權問題，沒有以一項實體裁決取代後來的政治安排。真正處理英國准入與冰島管轄權的，是一九七六年的英冰漁業協議：英國承認冰島二百海里經濟區，冰島則在指定海域、配額、船隻與漁具限制下，容許一定數量的英國漁船作業。Þór船長Ólafur Ólafsson的過失殺人指控亦以無罪告終。因而具體結果是冰島保住並擴大了二百海里管轄，英國取得受嚴格限制的漁業准入，海上對抗則以英方撤出爭議漁場、冰方停止攔截及外交協議取代。
resultEn: The practical cessation on 1 June did not produce a complete naval victory for either side. Iceland retained effective enforcement authority inside the fifty-mile zone. British trawlers largely withdrew from that area or resumed only restricted fishing under escort, while the British task force subsequently withdrew or redirected to other duties. On the same day that the confrontations ceased, Britain announced the establishment of its own two-hundred-mile fisheries protection zone, and Iceland likewise advanced its policy toward a two-hundred-mile jurisdiction. The dispute was then brought into International Court of Justice proceedings, where jurisdiction was considered before the practical issue was resolved by political agreement rather than a substantive judgment. The arrangement that ultimately dealt with British access and Icelandic jurisdiction was the 1976 Anglo-Icelandic fisheries agreement. Britain recognized Iceland's two-hundred-mile economic zone, while Iceland permitted a controlled amount of British fishing within designated areas, subject to quotas and limits on vessels and fishing gear. The manslaughter charge against Ólafur Ólafsson, captain of Þór, also ended in acquittal. The concrete outcome was therefore Icelandic control over a two-hundred-mile jurisdiction, regulated British access under the 1976 agreement, and the replacement of maritime confrontation with the withdrawal of British vessels from the disputed grounds, the end of Icelandic interceptions, and a bilateral settlement.
